::: {.callout-warning title="Preliminary output"}

This report is preliminary; all data and estimates in this study are provisional.
It documents the **recorded** Down syndrome (DS) population only — births with
`down_ind = 1` (`ca_down_c ∈ {C confirmed, P pending}`). The predicted-missing
extension and its demographic caveats are in
[`predicted.qmd`](predicted.qmd); the formal missed-case estimation is the
selection model. The full methods, query sketches, and benchmark-coverage caveats
are in the companion spec `docs/analysis/descriptive.md`.

:::

```{python}
# | echo: false
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown

config = json.loads(Path("config.json").read_text())


def _table(csv: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.read_csv(csv)


def _pct(frac: float) -> str:
    return f"{frac * 100:.1f}%"
```

```{python}
# | echo: false
Markdown(
    f"This report covers **{config['total_births']:,}** US live births "
    f"({config['year_min']}–{config['year_max']}), of which "
    f"**{config['total_recorded']:,}** were recorded with Down syndrome. "
    f"Against surveillance-expected counts the overall recording rate is "
    f"**{_pct(config['overall_recording_rate'])}** — i.e. roughly three in five "
    f"expected DS live births are absent from the birth certificate. "
    f"Generated {config['generated_at']}."
)
```

# Recorded numbers and trends

Recorded DS births run roughly flat-to-slightly-rising (~1.6k–2.2k per year)
against a *falling* total-birth denominator, so the rate per 10,000 rises faster
than the count. **"Pending" (`P`) exists only from 2004**, so the confirmed-only
line is the era-robust series; the confirmed + pending total has a step at the 2003
certificate change.

![Recorded DS live births by confirmation status, with the confirmed-only (era-robust) line and the 2003–2013 transition band.](recorded_confirmed_pending.png){#fig-confirmed-pending .lightbox fig-align="center"}

![Recorded DS per 10,000 live births. The level reflects recording completeness, not true prevalence (the surveillance benchmark is ≈ 13–14 per 10,000).](recorded_rate_per_10k.png){#fig-rate .lightbox fig-align="center"}

The "unknown" (`U`) and "not on certificate" (NULL) series are a data-quality
signal, not epidemiology — both spike around the 2003 cert changeover. The project
treats `U` and NULL as *not recorded*.

![DS item recorded as Unknown or absent from the certificate.](ds_status_unknown.png){#fig-unknown .lightbox fig-align="center"}

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | label: tbl-status
_status = _table("recorded_by_status.csv")
_disp = _status[
    ["year", "confirmed", "pending", "unknown", "not_on_cert", "births",
     "recorded_ds", "recorded_per_10k"]
].copy()
for c in ["confirmed", "pending", "unknown", "not_on_cert", "births", "recorded_ds"]:
    _disp[c] = _disp[c].map(lambda v: f"{int(v):,}")
_disp["recorded_per_10k"] = _disp["recorded_per_10k"].map(lambda v: f"{v:.2f}")
_disp = _disp.rename(columns={
    "year": "Year", "confirmed": "C", "pending": "P", "unknown": "U",
    "not_on_cert": "Not on cert", "births": "Births",
    "recorded_ds": "Recorded DS", "recorded_per_10k": "Per 10k",
}).set_index("Year")
_disp
```

# Recorded vs surveillance-expected

The gap between recorded bars and the expected lines is the under-reporting; the
ratio is the recording rate (≈ 40%). Expected counts come from the per-year
surveillance prevalence (`p_ds_lb_wt`) and the maternal-age Morris risk after
applying the year's termination/reduction rate (`p_ds_lb_nt_reduc`). The
surveillance tail (2018→2024) is carried forward and the reduction series is
extrapolated 2020–2024 — see the spec.

![Recorded vs surveillance-expected DS live births. Recorded bars sit well below every expected curve.](recorded_vs_expected.png){#fig-recorded-expected .lightbox fig-align="center"}

![Recording rate (recorded / expected) over time, against a ~36–43% reference band.](recording_rate_by_year.png){#fig-recording-rate .lightbox fig-align="center"}

Recording completeness is **not** uniform across groups. Using each group's
age-structure-adjusted expected count, recording rates differ markedly — a
differential-ascertainment signal (the de Graaf ethnicity benchmark, 2000–2018, is
an alternative external denominator described in the spec).

![Recording rate by maternal race / Hispanic origin over time (3-year rolling mean; age-risk expected denominator). The small AIAN group remains the most volatile.](recording_rate_by_race.png){#fig-recording-race .lightbox fig-align="center"}

# Maternal characteristics

Maternal age is the dominant DS risk axis: recorded DS prevalence rises steeply
with age, and recorded DS mothers are several years older on average than the
overall birth cohort — a gap that drifts as the whole cohort ages.

![Recorded DS rate by single-year maternal age.](recorded_ds_by_mage.png){#fig-mage .lightbox fig-align="center"}

![Mean and median maternal age: recorded DS births vs all births.](mean_mage_by_year.png){#fig-mean-age .lightbox fig-align="center"}

![Recorded DS births by maternal race / Hispanic origin (5-category; multi-race is identifiable only from 2014 and is not shown here).](recorded_ds_by_race.png){#fig-race-share .lightbox fig-align="center"}

Maternal education cannot be pooled across the 2003 certificate change (years of
schooling pre-2003 vs attainment level 2003+), so it is shown as two panels.

![Maternal education of recorded DS births over time — two non-poolable schemes (years of schooling, 1989–2002; attainment level, 2014–2024), each collapsed to four bands.](recorded_ds_by_education.png){#fig-education .lightbox fig-align="center"}

![Marital status of recorded DS mothers: share married (`dmar`/`mar` coalesced).](recorded_ds_by_marital.png){#fig-marital .lightbox fig-align="center"}

![Principal source of payment of recorded DS births over time (2014–2024).](recorded_ds_by_payer.png){#fig-payer .lightbox fig-align="center"}

# Pregnancy and infant characteristics

DS births skew towards lower birth weight and earlier gestation than the overall
cohort. Birth weight, gestation, and infant sex are 2003-certificate items
(`DBIRWT`/`GESTAT10`/`CSEX` pre-2003 are not loaded), so these begin in 2003.

![Birth weight: recorded DS vs all births (2003–2024).](recorded_ds_birthweight.png){#fig-birthweight .lightbox fig-align="center"}

![Gestational age: recorded DS vs all births (2003–2024).](recorded_ds_gestation.png){#fig-gestation .lightbox fig-align="center"}

![Infant sex: recorded DS births vs all births (typically developing), share male (2003–2024).](recorded_ds_sex.png){#fig-sex .lightbox fig-align="center"}

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | label: tbl-plurality
_plurality = _table("recorded_ds_plurality.csv")
_plurality["ds_n"] = _plurality["ds_n"].map(lambda v: f"{int(v):,}")
_plurality["ds_share"] = _plurality["ds_share"].map(_pct)
_plurality["all_share"] = _plurality["all_share"].map(_pct)
_plurality = _plurality.rename(columns={
    "plurality": "Plurality",
    "ds_n": "Recorded DS (n)",
    "ds_share": "Recorded DS (%)",
    "all_share": "All births / TD (%)",
})
_plurality[["Plurality", "Recorded DS (n)", "Recorded DS (%)", "All births / TD (%)"]].set_index("Plurality")
```

# Co-occurring conditions and newborn morbidity

Among recorded DS cases (2014–2024, `Y`/`N` base), co-occurring conditions are
noted far less often than clinical series report — birth-certificate checkbox
reporting under-ascertains, so each percentage is a **lower bound**. Cyanotic
congenital heart disease appears on a single-digit percentage of certificates,
against published congenital-heart-defect-in-DS estimates of ~40–50%; the
comparison is about the direction and magnitude of under-ascertainment, not exact
agreement.

![Co-occurring conditions among recorded DS births (2014–2024, % of the Y/N base).](recorded_ds_co_occurring.png){#fig-co-occurring .lightbox fig-align="center"}

```{python}
# | echo: false
# | label: tbl-co-occurring
_co = _table("recorded_ds_co_occurring.csv").sort_values("pct", ascending=False)
_co["pct"] = _co["pct"].map(lambda v: f"{v:.2f}%")
_co[["condition", "pct"]].rename(
    columns={"condition": "Condition", "pct": "% of recorded DS"}
).set_index("Condition")
```

![Newborn morbidity among recorded DS births over time (2014–2024).](recorded_ds_morbidity.png){#fig-morbidity .lightbox fig-align="center"}

# Limitations

The public-use file carries **no geography** (no state/county); it is **live
births only** (no terminations, so no antenatal prevalence); it has **no record
linkage** (no infant-death or longitudinal follow-up) and **no DS subtype**. Most
clinical detail (birth weight, gestation, sex, APGAR, and every 2003-cert
checkbox) is absent or non-comparable before 2003. Recorded cases are ≈ 40% of
expected and are likely severity-selected, so the characteristic distributions of
recorded cases need not match those of all DS births. See
`docs/analysis/descriptive.md` for the full limitations and the per-figure query
provenance, and [`predicted.qmd`](predicted.qmd) for the predicted-missing
extension.
